title: Deaerator
model_title: Deaerator (Spray-Tray Type) on Feedwater Storage Tank

introduction.definition: A deaerator removes dissolved oxygen and CO₂ from boiler feedwater. Water is sprayed into steam and cascades over trays, reaching saturation temperature so the gases are released and vented. The hot, deaerated water collects in the storage tank and feeds the boiler feed pumps.
applications: Power-station and industrial boiler feed systems
key_points: Hot (saturated) water holds almost no gas
Vent must show a small steam plume
introduction.summary: A deaerator removes dissolved oxygen and carbon dioxide from boiler feedwater, which would otherwise corrode the boiler. Incoming water is sprayed into steam and trickles over trays, heating it to saturation; the gases are released and vented, and the hot deaerated water collects in the storage tank.

foundation: Elevate the deaerator to give the feed pumps sufficient NPSH margin.
alignment: Check verticality (vertical vessels) or level and slope (horizontal); one saddle bolted, the other slotted for thermal expansion.
piping: Connect nozzles without forcing — check allowable nozzle loads; support piping independently.
Fit the required pressure relief device and isolation as per code.
commissioning: Hydro/pneumatic test per code; inspect internals before closing; purge and leak test; commission instruments and relief valves.

routine.task: Check vent plume, pressure and level.

lubrication: No lubrication — static equipment (lubricate valve stems and manway hinges only).

causes: Vent closed, low pressure, spray valve fault
remedies: Open vent, restore steam, repair valves

script.narration: This module introduces the Deaerator.
A deaerator removes dissolved oxygen and CO₂ from boiler feedwater.
Water is sprayed into steam and cascades over trays, reaching saturation temperature so the gases are released and vented.
The hot, deaerated water collects in the storage tank and feeds the boiler feed pumps.

video_tutorials.title: Deaerator — Operation

script.narration: How the Deaerator works.
Feedwater is sprayed into the deaerator head.
It cascades over the trays in counter-flow to rising steam.
Heated to saturation, the water releases O₂ and CO₂, which leave through the vent with a little steam.
Deaerated water collects in the storage tank.
The feed pumps draw from the bottom outlet.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Deaerator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Deaerator.
Check vent plume, pressure and level.
Measure dissolved O₂.
Inspect trays and spray valves.
Watch for high dissolved oxygen: O₂ above limit. Common cause: vent closed, low pressure, spray valve fault.
Watch for feed-pump cavitation: noise, low flow. Common cause: pressure decay on load change.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
